rules.title: A reference probability is given, or its absence is declared
rules.description: The record carries a baseline probability, or states that no baseline exists and why.
rules.rationale: Without a reference point, a prediction cannot be judged as informative. A 70 percent forecast is impressive against a base rate of 20 percent and worthless against a base rate of 70 percent, and the number alone does not say which.
rules.remediation: Record the base rate, naive forecast, or status-quo probability. If none exists, say so and explain why.

rules.title: The baseline names its source and its basis
rules.description: A stated baseline says where it came from and what population and period it is a rate over.
rules.rationale: A base rate is only a reference if you know what it is a rate of. The same event has different base rates across different populations, and a baseline without that context can be chosen after the fact to make a prediction look good.
rules.remediation: State the source and describe the population and period the rate covers.
rules.$assuranceNote: The evaluator observes that a source and basis were written. It cannot check that the population described is the relevant one for this prediction.
